Freya, the goddess of love, beauty, fertility, magic, and war—embodying the full range of female power in Norse mythology. She is the sister of Frey and a member of the Vanir, the fertility gods who merged with the Aesir after their ancient truce. Unlike the gentler Frey, Freya blends both the tender and the martial, neither purely gentle nor purely violent, but complex and whole.

She wears the necklace Brisingamen, crafted by dwarves and representing her dominion over beauty and desire. She owns the golden boar Hildisvíni and travels in a chariot drawn by cats, symbols of independence and magic. Freya is skilled in seidr, a form of prophecy and magic that allowed her to see and shape fate itself—a mastery that rivals even Odin's own magical knowledge.

In matters of war and honor, she claims half of all warriors who die honorably in battle for her hall Folkvangr. She and Odin divide the slain between them, with Odin taking the other half. This authority positions her as a rival and partner to Odin himself in commanding the honored dead. Through the Valkyries, she extends her influence and her claims across the battlefields of the world.

Freya shares connections to many in the Norse pantheon: her brother Frey, the Aesir queen Frigg, and even the trickster Loki, whose schemes sometimes attempt to steal her treasured necklace.
